blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Harlequin ichthyosis due to biallelic loss of ABCA12 function — ABCA12 is an ATP-binding cassette lipid transporter in epidermal keratinocytes that is critical for lamellar-granule lipid delivery to the stratum corneum. Severe loss of ABCA12 function disrupts lipid transport and extracellular lipid-barrier formation, producing marked hyperkeratosis and a profoundly impaired epidermal barrier.
official_outline_path: Harlequin ichthyosis — ABCA12-mediated epidermal lipid transport defect
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. Transglutaminase 1 defects are a classic cause of lamellar ichthyosis and impair cornified-envelope formation, but the severe harlequin phenotype with biallelic ABCA12 loss is caused by defective epidermal lipid transport.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. Steroid sulfatase deficiency causes X-linked ichthyosis, characterized by retention hyperkeratosis from cholesterol sulfate accumulation; it does not explain the ABCA12-associated lamellar-granule lipid-transport defect.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The newborn has harlequin ichthyosis. ABCA12 encodes an ATP-binding cassette lipid transporter in keratinocytes. Severe loss of ABCA12 function disrupts lipid trafficking through lamellar granules and lipid delivery to the stratum corneum, preventing normal extracellular lipid-barrier formation. The resulting barrier failure and abnormal cornification produce the thick plate-like hyperkeratosis, fissuring, ectropion, eclabium, dehydration risk, and susceptibility to infection.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. Filaggrin loss is associated with ichthyosis vulgaris and atopic barrier dysfunction, not the characteristic neonatal armor-like plates of severe ABCA12 deficiency.
distractor_explanations.E: Incorrect. KRT1/KRT10 defects cause epidermolytic ichthyosis through keratin cytoskeletal fragility; that mechanism differs from the lamellar-granule lipid transport failure caused by ABCA12 loss.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Congenital afibrinogenemia — Congenital afibrinogenemia is a severe quantitative fibrinogen disorder, usually autosomal recessive, caused by pathogenic variants affecting fibrinogen-chain genes or fibrinogen synthesis/assembly/secretion. Near-absence of circulating fibrinogen prevents normal fibrin clot formation, causing marked prolongation of fibrin-dependent clotting assays.
blueprint.primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. Hemophilia A causes factor VIII deficiency and typically produces an isolated prolongation of the activated partial thromboplastin time with a normal prothrombin time and normal fibrinogen level.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. Factor XIII stabilizes fibrin after the initial clot forms. Factor XIII deficiency can cause delayed bleeding and umbilical stump bleeding, but routine PT, aPTT, and thrombin time are typically normal because these assays end before factor XIII-mediated cross-linking.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. von Willebrand disease impairs platelet adhesion and can reduce factor VIII stability. PT is normal and fibrinogen is not absent; aPTT may be normal or prolonged depending on factor VIII levels.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. Dysfibrinogenemia is a qualitative fibrinogen defect. Functional activity is disproportionately reduced relative to antigen concentration; complete absence of both functional fibrinogen and fibrinogen antigen is characteristic of afibrinogenemia.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. The infant has congenital afibrinogenemia. The decisive laboratory pattern is undetectable fibrinogen activity and antigen together with marked prolongation of PT, aPTT, and thrombin time, all of which ultimately depend on fibrin formation. Umbilical bleeding is a classic early presentation. Hemophilia A affects the intrinsic pathway, factor XIII deficiency occurs after fibrin formation and therefore does not prolong routine clotting times, von Willebrand disease does not eliminate fibrinogen, and dysfibrinogenemia is primarily a qualitative rather than complete quantitative fibrinogen defect.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase deficiency (PORD) — POR transfers electrons from NADPH to microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes in the endoplasmic reticulum, including CYP17A1, CYP21A2, and CYP19A1. Loss of POR therefore produces a combined steroidogenic defect rather than deficiency of a single adrenal enzyme.
official_outline_path: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia / disorders of steroid biosynthesis
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. StAR deficiency impairs mitochondrial cholesterol delivery and broadly reduces steroidogenesis, but it does not explain the characteristic combined microsomal P450 defect caused by POR loss.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. PORD is caused by pathogenic variants in POR, which encodes the flavoprotein electron donor for microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes. POR accepts electrons from NADPH and transfers them to enzymes including CYP17A1, CYP21A2, and CYP19A1. Consequently, POR deficiency can mimic a combination of 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase and 21-hydroxylase deficiencies and can also impair aromatase activity, helping explain genital atypia and maternal virilization.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. Ferredoxin-dependent electron transfer supports mitochondrial steroidogenic P450 enzymes. POR instead supplies electrons to microsomal P450 enzymes in the endoplasmic reticulum.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. HSD3B2 deficiency blocks conversion of pregnenolone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone, and DHEA to their Δ4 products; it is a single-enzyme defect, not a shared electron-donor defect affecting several microsomal P450 enzymes.
distractor_explanations.E: Incorrect. CYP21A2 deficiency can cause congenital adrenal hyperplasia but cannot explain simultaneous impairment of CYP17A1 and aromatase-related pathways.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2 (HSD3B2) deficiency — HSD3B2 converts Δ5 steroids to Δ4 steroids in adrenal cortex and gonads: pregnenolone to progesterone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone to 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and DHEA to androstenedione. Deficiency reduces glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, and gonadal sex-steroid synthesis and raises Δ5 precursors.
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. This describes 21-hydroxylase activity; its deficiency characteristically raises 17-hydroxyprogesterone rather than producing a generalized Δ5-to-Δ4 conversion defect.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. HSD3B2 is expressed in adrenal cortex and gonads and is required for the Δ5-to-Δ4 conversion of several steroid intermediates. It converts pregnenolone to progesterone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone to 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and DHEA to androstenedione. Severe deficiency therefore produces low cortisol and aldosterone, impaired androgen synthesis in 46,XY infants, salt wasting, and accumulation of Δ5 precursors.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. This describes 17,20-lyase activity of CYP17A1. The stem instead shows accumulation of multiple Δ5 steroids with low corresponding Δ4 products.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. This describes 11β-hydroxylase activity. Deficiency would raise 11-deoxysteroids and commonly produce mineralocorticoid hypertension rather than this pattern.
distractor_explanations.E: Incorrect. 5α-reductase acts peripherally on testosterone and does not cause combined adrenal salt wasting with accumulation of pregnenolone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone, and DHEA.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Therapeutic silence during emotional disclosure — A deliberate period of attentive silence can communicate presence, avoid interrupting emotional processing, and give the patient time to reflect or continue speaking; it is especially appropriate immediately after an emotionally intense disclosure or while a patient is crying.
blueprint.primary_competency: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
blueprint.primary_system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. Immediate task-focused questioning interrupts emotional processing and shifts away from the concern the patient has just disclosed.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. Uncertain prognostic reassurance can be false reassurance and does not respond to the patient's immediate emotion.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. Changing the subject avoids rather than acknowledges the emotional content of the encounter.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. Normalization can sometimes be helpful, but immediately continuing without allowing space ignores the patient's current emotional processing.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. After an emotionally intense disclosure and while the patient is crying, a brief period of attentive silence is an appropriate therapeutic communication technique. Shared silence can support reflection and emotional processing while communicating that the clinician is willing to remain present. Once the patient is ready, the clinician can resume with gentle exploration or empathic reflection.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Mucolipidosis II alpha/beta (I-cell disease) due to GNPTAB deficiency — GNPTAB encodes the alpha/beta subunits of N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase, which initiates mannose-6-phosphate targeting of lysosomal hydrolases in the Golgi. Loss of this enzyme causes lysosomal enzymes to be missorted and secreted extracellularly rather than delivered efficiently to lysosomes.
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. A receptor-binding defect could also disturb lysosomal targeting, but mucolipidosis II from GNPTAB loss is caused upstream by failure of the phosphotransferase-mediated tagging step.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. Lysosomal acidification defects impair enzyme function after delivery; they do not explain secretion of many hydrolases into plasma due to missorting in the Golgi.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. Autophagosome-lysosome fusion defects affect autophagic degradation but are not the primary GNPTAB trafficking lesion.
distractor_explanations.D: Incorrect. Defective proenzyme processing would occur after lysosomal delivery and would not produce the characteristic broad extracellular elevation of lysosomal hydrolases.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Mucolipidosis II alpha/beta is a GNPTAB-related lysosomal trafficking disorder. GNPTAB encodes N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphotransferase alpha/beta subunits. Loss of phosphotransferase activity prevents appropriate Golgi targeting modification of lysosomal hydrolases, causing missorting and extracellular secretion rather than normal lysosomal delivery. This explains high plasma hydrolase activity despite intracellular lysosomal deficiency.

distractor_explanations.A: Incorrect. UGT1A1-mediated bilirubin conjugation is unrelated to CYP7A1-dependent cholesterol catabolism.
distractor_explanations.B: Incorrect. MRP2 mediates canalicular bilirubin transport and is defective in Dubin-Johnson syndrome, not CYP7A1 deficiency.
distractor_explanations.C: Incorrect. MTTP is required for ApoB lipoprotein assembly and is defective in abetalipoproteinemia.

Deficiency decreases conversion of cholesterol to bile acids and reduces a major route of cholesterol elimination. Human CYP7A1 deficiency has been associated with high LDL cholesterol, deficient bile-acid excretion, premature gallstones, and premature vascular disease.

options.A: Conjugation of bilirubin with glucuronic acid in hepatocytes
options.B: Canalicular export of conjugated bilirubin through MRP2
options.C: Microsomal transfer of triglyceride onto nascent apolipoprotein B
options.D: 7alpha-hydroxylation of cholesterol during the initial step of the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway
options.E: Conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate during cholesterol synthesis

item.tested_construct: CYP7A1 encodes cholesterol 7alpha-hydroxylase, which catalyzes the initial and rate-controlling step of the classic bile-acid synthesis pathway from cholesterol. Loss of CYP7A1 reduces bile-acid production and cholesterol catabolism, promoting hepatic cholesterol accumulation, increased LDL cholesterol, and gallstone/atherosclerotic risk.
item.vignette: A 32-year-old man has severe hypercholesterolemia despite adherence to a statin. He developed cholesterol gallstones in his twenties, and his father had premature coronary artery disease. Liver testing shows markedly reduced bile-acid synthesis. Genetic analysis identifies a homozygous loss-of-function variant in CYP7A1.

Deficiency decreases conversion of cholesterol to bile acids and reduces a major route of cholesterol elimination. Human CYP7A1 deficiency has been associated with high LDL cholesterol, deficient bile-acid excretion, premature gallstones, and premature vascular disease.
